headline: The stolen-wallet case can be worked out, but two rules in one document conflict over a pending refund, and the grade also depends on freezing the cards before closing them.

issues.summary: The Green account's only blocker is a pending refund row. That row is both a 'pending transaction' (req 4, absolute block) and a 'pending refund' (req 5, waivable by written acknowledgment). Gold applies req 5 and closes and reissues the card.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025 req 4: "No pending transactions: The card must not have any pending or processing transactions."
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025 req 5: "No pending refunds ... or acknowledge in writing that the refunds will be credited to the linked checking account instead."
task_079 initial_state btxn_d0b8b00ed468: type="refund", status="pending", account chk_cr89a2b3c4_3
gold[19] close_debit_card_4721 dbc_cr89a2b3c4_green; gold[24] order_debit_card_5739 chk_cr89a2b3c4_3 STANDARD
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that reads req 4 literally refuses to close the Green card, so the close and order are missing and the hash differs. The more specific req 5 is the intended reading and the customer script supports the acknowledgment, so most careful agents get there.
issues.suggested_fix: State in req 4 that pending refunds are governed by req 5 instead.

issues.summary: Freezing a lost/stolen card leaves 'frozen_date' and 'unfrozen_date' fields on the card record, and a frozen card must be unfrozen before close_debit_card_4721 will accept it, so the final DB depends on whether the agent froze first. Doc 026 tells agents to recommend closing instead of freezing once loss/theft is confirmed, which gives a second defensible path with a different final state.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026: "If customer confirms the card is lost/stolen, recommend closing instead of freezing"
tools.py freeze_debit_card_3892: card["frozen_date"] = get_today_str(); unfreeze_debit_card_3893: card["unfrozen_date"] = get_today_str()
tools.py close_debit_card_4721: "Only ACTIVE or PENDING cards can be closed."
task_079 instructions step 1: "I need to freeze all my debit cards immediately." (theft already confirmed in the opening)
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that follows doc 026, recommends closing outright, and gets the simulated customer's agreement (the script says to follow the agent's guidance) closes the cards without the freeze/unfreeze round trip. Its card records then lack the two date fields and the unfreeze tool is never logged, so the hash differs from gold. A replay that drops the freeze/unfreeze calls for the closed cards confirmed the mismatch for task_078. The customer's explicit opening request to freeze makes the gold path the usual one, so this is rated Minor.
issues.suggested_fix: Exclude transient freeze bookkeeping fields (frozen_date/unfrozen_date) from the hash, or have close_debit_card_4721 accept FROZEN cards and clear those fields, so both paths converge.

solution_check: Independently: freeze all three. Transactions show no pending rows on Evergreen or Light Blue, and only the pending refund on Green. Light Blue has two 'lost' replacements within 12 months (04/05/2025, 08/10/2025), so it is at the ENTRY limit. The customer accepts the $25 fee, but the ENTRY 48-hour post-closure wait still blocks the order. Evergreen is PREMIUM: RUSH $35 and PREMIUM design $0. Green is MID: STANDARD/CLASSIC (metallic costs $10, which the customer declines). Unfreezing and closing all three as 'stolen' and ordering Evergreen and Green matches gold exactly, and gold replays without errors.
prior_note: The prior review rated this clean. #402 only added a gold get_all_user_accounts read. Both Minor issues are newly reported.
notes: Grading-model facts confirmed against the v1.0.1 snapshot: EnvironmentEvaluator replays gold on a fresh env and compares get_db_hash/get_user_db_hash (both hash the same TransactionalDB here because KnowledgeUserTools shares the agent db); _derive_read_log_allowlist logs discoverable reads only when the gold calls that tool name; the agent_discoverable_tools record id is derived from the tool name only, so the log is a set (call count and arguments do not matter), and write-tool calls are logged even when the tool returns an 'Error:' string; call_discoverable_agent_tool parses arguments with json.loads(parse_int=float); get_now() is fixed at 2025-11-14 03:40. The refund row's type 'refund' is not in doc 018's documented type enum (fee_refund is), a cosmetic data inconsistency.
